text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers.
- Government will allow private companies to develop two-thirds of next year's batch of executive condominiums in seven sites.
- UN General Assembly endorses Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, banning nuclear explosions in the atmosphere, underground or any other environment.
- More Singaporeans receive government help to pay hospital bills.
- Prices for next batch of executive condiminiums may remain at about Singapore $400 psf because of "certain inherent factors".
- American electronics firm, Whirpool Corp, is retrenching 150 of its staff here with its shutdown of research and development centre and relocation of regional headquarters to Hongkong.
- ASEAN Agreement on Customs cooperation finalised by member countries' top customs officials.
- Indonesian central bank to widen rupiah-US dollar intervention band from 5 per cent to 8 per cent.
- Oil prices soar to highest level since Gulf War on news Iraq fired at US fighter planes flying over north of the country.
- Diversified conglomerate Renong Bhd is leading a consortium to take over Malaysia national railway company Keratapi Tanah Melayu.
- Specialist engineering company Presscrete Engineering will launch an IPO to raise funds for expansion here and in Malaysia.
